boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Uptown-campus places for studying, meeting, making, recreation, and taking in art.

cards.title: Howard-Tilton Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Central Uptown campus library
cards.notes: Use the seven-floor library as a starting point for coursework, then choose a collaborative or quiet area that fits the task at hand.
cards.short_summary: A large academic library with varied study settings and support spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane describes Howard-Tilton as a seven-floor Uptown-campus library with seating for more than 1,100 users, classrooms, and specialized study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours; after 7 p.m., entry is limited to active Tulane affiliates with Tulane ID.

cards.title: Learning Commons at Howard-Tilton
cards.subtitle: First floor, Howard-Tilton Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a group project or research question here for collaborative seating, technology resources, printing, power, and nearby help.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative first-floor work area inside Howard-Tilton.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons offers individual and group work areas, wireless, printers, power outlets, research support, and technology resources.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Howard-Tilton; follow library building-access policies and current hours.

cards.title: Selley Study Commons
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Howard-Tilton Memorial Library
cards.notes: Choose this third-floor area when you need individual, quiet work; use its carrels, pod workstations, or lounge seating.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study area with several individual seating formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane Libraries identifies the Selley Study Commons as a quiet third-floor space designed for quiet, individual study.
cards.access_notes: Group work is not permitted in this quiet-study area; check current library access policies.

cards.title: Library Classroom 430
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor, Howard-Tilton Memorial Library
cards.notes: Check whether no library class or event is scheduled, then use the open classroom’s tables and outlets as a study area.
cards.short_summary: A glassed-in fourth-floor classroom that is available for student study when unscheduled.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane Libraries says Classroom 430 is open for student study without reservations when no classes or events are scheduled.
cards.source_title: New Library Classroom and Event Space Can Be Used for Studying Too
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on library classes and events; rooms are otherwise reserved for Tulane instruction and events.

cards.title: James Lounge
cards.subtitle: First level, Lavin-Bernick Center
cards.notes: Settle into the soft seating, tables, or bar-height seats for a conversation or a short study session near McAlister Way.
cards.short_summary: A first-level LBC lounge overlooking campus activity along McAlister Way.
cards.evidence_claim: The LBC describes James Lounge as a first-level lounge with soft seating, tables, lounges, and bar seating.
cards.source_title: Lounges + Study Spaces | The Lavin-Bernick Center
cards.access_notes: Inside the LBC, behind FedEx/Kinko's; consult current LBC building hours.

cards.title: Rosenberg Mezzanine
cards.subtitle: Between the first and second levels of the LBC
cards.notes: Use the mezzanine’s mix of soft seating, lounges, and tables for an informal check-in, reading break, or solo work.
cards.short_summary: A seating-filled LBC mezzanine between its first and second levels.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane’s LBC lists the Rosenberg Mezzanine as offering soft seating, lounges, and tables.
cards.source_title: Lounges + Study Spaces | The Lavin-Bernick Center
cards.access_notes: Inside the Lavin-Bernick Center; LBC lists general building hours as 7 a.m.–11 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Student Organization Center
cards.subtitle: Room G11, Garden Level, Lavin-Bernick Center
cards.notes: Recognized student organizations can use this hub for small meetings, materials, printing, storage, package pickup, and project making.
cards.short_summary: A resource and meeting hub for Tulane’s recognized student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane says recognized student organizations can meet, make posters and buttons, print, store items, and receive packages in the Student Organization Center.
cards.access_notes: Located in LBC G11; after-hours and weekend access requires an organization request and is limited.

cards.title: Pocket Park
cards.subtitle: Lavin-Bernick Center outdoor event area
cards.notes: Look for registered campus events here, or have your recognized organization reserve the space through the university’s event process.
cards.short_summary: An LBC-managed outdoor venue used for campus meetings and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lavin-Bernick Center lists Pocket Park among its event locations, with capacity for 200 and reservations handled through EMS.
cards.access_notes: Event use requires a reservation; respect posted event setups and campus policies.

cards.title: Newcomb Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Woldenberg Art Center, 50 Newcomb Place
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit around current exhibition hours, then use the museum’s collection and programs as a focused campus arts stop.
cards.short_summary: Tulane’s on-campus art museum facing Newcomb Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Newcomb Art Museum is located in Woldenberg Art Center on Tulane’s Uptown campus, directly facing Newcomb Quad.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Saturday 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm closures before visiting.

cards.title: Newcomb Quad
cards.subtitle: Uptown campus green beside Dixon Hall
cards.notes: Use the quad as an outdoor meeting point when campus programming is underway, and follow event signage and any space-reservation boundaries.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor gathering space used for Tulane community programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane’s commUNITY program used Dixon Hall and Newcomb Quad for an event centering student, faculty, and staff voices and campus connection.
cards.source_title: commUNITY | Office of Academic Excellence and Opportunity
cards.access_notes: Outdoor programming and access can vary with weather, reservations, and university events.
